site.title: Model validation
site.intro: Reports on how well my models hold up when they are tested on data they have not seen, written to be read next to one another.

rules.name: Gates before results
rules.text: An idea is accepted only if it beats its reference under a rule written before the run. Failed gates are published with the passed ones.

rules.name: Splits that match the use
rules.text: Nested cross-validation on the population that will be scored, and scaffold splits when the model will meet new chemistry, with the random-split number shown beside it.

rules.name: Uncertainty on every number
rules.text: Intervals, the size of the held-out set and the fraction of censored values are reported with each estimate.

rules.name: Controls that can fail
rules.text: Permuted-label controls and independent data that the method was never fitted to, so that a leak or a weak metric shows up.

rules.name: Regenerated from the data
rules.text: Each figure is produced from files in a public repository, and an audit rebuilds the reported numbers and compares them with the text.

reports.title: CYP3A4 structure entry against the Boltz-2 baseline
reports.summary: A restrained co-folding entry scores 0.413 LDDT-PLI, indistinguishable from the published baseline at 0.420.
body: The entry used Boltz-2 co-folding with a restraint that pulls a ligand nitrogen toward the heme iron. After the deadline the organisers released the crystal structures, which made a direct comparison possible.

The entry cannot be told apart from the baseline. If the best of the poses generated for each compound had been chosen instead, the mean score would have been 0.526, so most of the gap lies in choosing the pose and not in generating it. A different selection threshold would have added at most 0.034, against a gap of 0.126 to the first place.

The restraint found all four ligands that coordinate the iron in the crystals. It also placed a nitrogen close to the iron for eight further ligands (2.75 to 4.93 Å in the released structures), which the crystals do not show.
reports.caption: Mean LDDT-PLI over the scored ligands. The last bar is an upper bound that needs the answer to choose the pose; it is not an achievable score.

reports.title: Time-dependent inhibition: nested cross-validation and the final board
reports.summary: Nested cross-validation on the scored population gives AUC 0.73 to 0.86; the blind board scored macro MCC 0.372 and 14th of 62.
body: Model selection and the reported AUC come from separate loops. The inner loop picks the model and its calibration; the outer loop, which never influenced either choice, is what the figures below report.
The two label thresholds tried (z0 = 1.96 and 1.0) change the AUC by 0.02 to 0.03 for either enzyme. CYP2D6 is the harder endpoint at both.
reports.caption: Outer-loop AUC of nested cross-validation on the scored population.

reports.title: A selection-aware CYP2D6 model
reports.summary: Modelling how compounds came to be tested raises CYP2D6 AUC from 0.562 to 0.728 on a set that resembles the training panel.
body: Compounds were not tested on every enzyme at random, so the labels that exist are a selected sample. A model of that selection improved CYP2D6 on a scored set that looks like the training panel.
Which file to submit was decided by a rule written before any upload. A hedged blend of the hits-only and selection-aware stacks was tried as well and did not pass its gate.
reports.caption: AUC on a scored set that resembles the training panel.

reports.title: Calibration of the published probabilities
reports.summary: Isotonic calibration brings the expected calibration error to 0.019 for CYP3A4 and 0.005 for CYP2D6; the raw CYP2D6 blend was a ranking, not a probability.

headline.label: ECE of the raw CYP2D6 blend

body: A calibration method was accepted only if the expected calibration error was at most 0.05 and the calibration slope lay between 0.8 and 1.2, with the choice made on the inner folds.

The raw output of the CYP2D6 blend fails that gate by a wide margin. It ranks compounds and transfers a call rate, but its numbers are not probabilities until calibrated, and the report states this as a limitation.
reports.caption: Expected calibration error; lower is better.

explore.title: Explore the calibration
explore.lede: The methods that were tried for each enzyme, at the gate that a probability had to meet: an expected calibration error of at most 0.05 and a slope between 0.8 and 1.2.

reports.title: Negative control on permuted labels
reports.summary: With the labels permuted and the whole nested procedure repeated, the outer AUC is 0.510 and 0.501, as chance requires.
body: A pipeline that tunes many choices can find signal in noise. The control permutes the labels of the pool and repeats the entire nested procedure, including model selection. A result near 0.5 shows that the procedure itself does not leak.
reports.caption: Outer AUC on permuted labels at z0 = 1.0.

reports.title: Estimating the positive rate without a board
reports.summary: A label-shift estimate that reads no leaderboard is too wide to confirm or contradict the board-derived rates.
body: The one piece of aggregate information about the hidden labels that the entry uses is the positive rate of the scored set, which the public boards make recoverable. A second estimate, from a classifier that scores held-out compounds and the blinded structures on one scale and reads no board, checks that rate.
Under the rule fixed before the first run, both verdicts are NOT INFORMATIVE. Each interval contains the board-derived rate, so the check neither supports nor contradicts it.
reports.caption: Estimated positive rate with its interval, against the rate recovered from the boards.

reports.title: The ledger of 187 gates
reports.summary: Every idea had to beat its reference under a rule fixed before the run. Nine of 187 verdicts were met; the 178 that were not are published.
body: Each addition had to beat its reference at a corrected significance level, alone and inside the final stack, under a rule fixed before the run. The count of 187 is the one number that every document of the project quotes for what was tried.
An audit regenerates every reported number from the data on a clean clone and compares it with the text. The ledger of failed gates is part of the repository, not an appendix to it.
reports.caption: One square per verdict. Filled: gate met.

reports.title: Scaffold split against random split for BBB permeability
reports.summary: Fingerprint and graph networks score 0.95 or higher on a random split and 0.60 to 0.69 when whole ring systems are held out.

headline.label: fingerprint network, scaffold split (95% CI 0.53 to 0.68)
graph network, scaffold split (95% CI 0.61 to 0.76)

body: A stratified random split lets the same ring systems appear in training and test, which is not the situation of a new drug candidate. The scaffold split removes every test ring system from training, and the deployed models are trained and scored that way.

The random-split figure that the project used to quote overstated how well the fingerprint model handles new chemistry. The intervals overlap, so the better result of the graph model is a data point, not a verdict.
reports.caption: ROC-AUC on 204 held-out compounds; the bar around the scaffold value is its 95% interval. Random-split values are the approximate figures in the README.

reports.title: Peptide developability metrics against measured safety data
reports.summary: Aggregation propensity and solubility track measured cytotoxicity of 215 designed peptides, but not hemolysis, where half the values are censored.
datasets: Measured safety data for 217 designed antimicrobial peptides

headline.label: aggregation propensity against measured β-sheet content

body: The two metrics were not fitted to these data. The measurements are an independent test of whether the heuristics track anything real.

Both metrics correlate with cytotoxicity in the expected direction. Neither correlates significantly with hemolysis (p between 0.09 and 0.18), but 50.2% of hemolysis values are recorded as above the assay ceiling, so that null carries real uncertainty. The tool reports the censored fraction beside every correlation.

Aggregation propensity correlates negatively with measured β-sheet content, the opposite of what its source on amyloid formation would predict. The most likely reading is that, for helical antimicrobial peptides, the metric tracks membrane-disruptive character and not β-sheet aggregation, which argues for renaming or reworking it.
reports.caption: Spearman correlation coefficients, n = 215 peptides with measurements.
